title: Carissimi et al. (2021): human miRNA (h)m5C mapping
text: BS-miRNA-seq and MAmBA map cytosine modifications in human miRNAs. Bisulfite non-conversion does not by itself distinguish m5C from hm5C. The project curated position-resolved mature-miRNA records; use each atlas record's matching mature arm, nucleotide position and source table rather than assigning this paper to every site in a miRNA family. Antibody validation supports both modifications in mature miRNAs, not automatic chemical identification of every individual called site.

title: Konno et al. (2019): mature miRNAs in gastrointestinal cancer
text: The project's curated master records targeted MALDI-TOF-MS/MS evidence for miR-200c-3p mature C9 and miR-21-5p mature C9. These are specific miRNA/site records, not evidence that all cytosines or both arms are methylated. Interpret tissue, serum and disease observations in the study's sample context. The curated notes flag a miR-21 arm-label inconsistency in the article text; the supplementary MS/MS evidence identifies 5p.

title: Cheray et al. (2020): miRNA methylation in glioblastoma
text: The curated project records distinguish exact mature-nucleotide evidence, candidate CpG position sets from small-RNA bisulfite sequencing, and nonpositional anti-m5C immunoprecipitation array enrichment. A miRNA-level array result is not proof of a particular C position. Candidate CpG summaries from three U87 replicates must not be reported as independently measured methylation rates for every candidate nucleotide. Preserve the resolution attached to each source record.

title: Ohshiro et al. (2021): single-molecule RNA modification detection
text: Single-molecule RNA sequencing was investigated for simultaneous detection of m6A and 5mC. The project's curated master includes five exact mature-nucleotide records from this study. Consult an exact matched atlas citation before claiming a particular miRNA position; do not extrapolate a demonstrated method to all small RNAs.

title: Lü et al. (2024): purified mature-miRNA LC-MS/MS
text: Two-step hybridization purification was coupled to LC-MS/MS to measure modifications in mature miRNAs. The project's curated records classify this evidence as miRNA-level and nonpositional. Modified nucleoside abundance in purified RNA does not alone identify a modified nucleotide coordinate.

title: Zeng et al.: miRNAs in minimal change disease
text: The project's curated master includes 83 miRNA-level, nonpositional records under this publication, labeled 2026 in the local bibliography (PMID 41235950). Use the source publication for publication-date details. These records are not exact nucleotide validation and cannot establish that an arbitrary atlas C site was previously reported. This entry is a pointer to the locally curated literature, not an independently revalidated site map.

title: Haag et al. (2015): NSUN6 and tRNA C72
text: Human NSUN6 methylates C72 in specific tRNA-Cys and tRNA-Thr substrates. Recognition depends on the 3-prime CCA tail in the reported in-vitro experiments. This finding should not be generalized to every tRNA with cytosine at that coordinate. Use mature-tRNA numbering and species-specific substrate identity.

title: NSUN2-dependent methylation and tRNA fragmentation (2014)
text: Loss of NSUN2-dependent cytosine methylation increased angiogenin-mediated tRNA cleavage and accumulation of 5-prime tRNA fragments in the studied human and mouse systems, with effects on translation and cellular stress. Modification on a parental tRNA and detection in a tRNA-derived fragment are related but distinct observations. Do not infer a causal cleavage mechanism from one atlas call alone.

title: Human DNMT2 and tRNA-Asp C38 (2008)
text: Human DNMT2 catalyzes methylation of C38 in tRNA-Asp using a DNA-methyltransferase-like catalytic mechanism. DNMT2 is also known as TRDMT1. Cite substrate-specific experiments; this evidence does not assign DNMT2 as the writer for all small-RNA m5C sites.

title: NSUN3 and ALKBH1: mitochondrial tRNA-Met modification pathway (2016)
text: NSUN3 introduces m5C34 in mitochondrial tRNA-Met and ALKBH1/ABH1 oxidizes it to f5C34, expanding codon recognition. A signal at this coordinate must be interpreted with the assay's chemical specificity: pathway involvement does not prove the endpoint is unoxidized m5C. Distinguish mitochondrial tRNA-Met from cytoplasmic tRNA-Met.

title: NSUN5 and ribosomal RNA methylation (2019)
text: NSUN5 introduces m5C at human 28S rRNA C3782 and mouse 28S rRNA C3438 in the reported study. The species and reference numbering matter. A short RNA read assigned to rRNA may derive from a large rRNA precursor; do not classify the intact 28S molecule as a small RNA or transfer a coordinate between species without mapping.

title: TAPS chemistry: original DNA method (2019)
text: The original DNA TAPS method uses TET oxidation of 5mC/5hmC to 5caC and pyridine-borane reduction to dihydrouracil, producing C-to-T readout. It is a DNA study, not experimental validation of the project's RNA adaptation. Treat the sRNA-TAPS documentation as the source for its RNA workflow and controls; do not equate the two validation scopes.

title: Pyridine-borane readout and RNA oxidation products (2022)
text: Reactivity-dependent profiling of RNA 5-methylcytidine dioxygenases investigated RNA oxidation products and pyridine-borane-based readout, including mitochondrial tRNA-Met. Native oxidized cytosines can matter for interpretation of a conversion signal. Use the actual treatment and control scheme rather than labeling every C-to-T event as chemically specific m5C.
